passage:
Neelam had run every morning for forty-one days, and her phone app showed the unbroken line of dots. On day forty-two her right knee began to ache on the stairs. She told herself it was just stiffness.

Her friend Vishal, running beside her, said, "You're limping. Stop for today." She shook her head. "I'm not losing the streak." She ran the full loop, her jaw set.

By the weekend she could not bend the knee without wincing. The doctor told her to rest completely. Neelam missed the weeks she had been so afraid to miss, and stared at the app's blank squares, thinking how the streak she protected had cost her the running itself.

What was Neelam feeling when she shook her head at Vishal?
qa.a: Neelam was determined and afraid of losing the streak, so pride and fear pushed her to ignore the pain.

qa.q: What could Neelam do when she can run again, and why?
qa.a: Neelam could allow rest days and stop at the first sign of pain, because the aim is running for the long term and not a perfect chain of dots.

qa.a: Vishal was probably worried and frustrated, having said clearly that she was limping, and felt helpless as she carried on.

grounding: Determined not to lose a streak, the person ignores knee pain and keeps running, and the injury stops training for weeks.

"You're limping," Uday said, as Vinita came in from her run.
"It's nothing. My knee's been clicking."
"Since when?"
"Since last week." She sat down carefully. "Day forty-two of my streak. I'm not breaking it."
"Vinita, you winced on the stairs."
"Everyone's knees hurt when they run."
The next morning she ran again. Uday heard her come back slower than usual and put ice on it without saying anything.
Four days later she couldn't bend her leg at all. At the physiotherapist's that evening, she came out with a brace and a printout.
"Well?" Uday asked.
"No running for at least six weeks. Exercises only." She threw the brace on the sofa. "Forty-six days. And now zero."
"If you'd rested last week?"
She didn't answer. She just stared at the printout.

qa.q: What did Vinita bring home from the physiotherapist?
qa.a: She came out with a brace and a printout.

qa.q: What was Vinita feeling when she refused to break her streak?
qa.a: She felt stubbornly determined and proud of forty-two days, which made her brush off the pain.

qa.q: What approach would have protected both Vinita's knee and her habit?
qa.a: Resting and getting the knee checked when it first clicked would have cost a few days, not six weeks.

qa.q: How does Uday feel watching this happen?
qa.a: Uday seems worried from the start, noticing the limp and the wince, and quietly helps with ice even though she won't listen.

grounding: Shows a person ignoring knee pain to keep a running streak, leading to an injury that stops training for weeks.

subtype: Approach: push through pain to keep the streak [Pitfall]
passage:
I was on day sixty of my morning run streak when my left knee started aching. Sixty days. I'd posted about it in my college group. My friend Zubin, who plays football, told me to take a few days off and get it seen. I laughed. "Pain is just weakness leaving."
So I kept going. I switched to the flatter route, taped my knee, and ran slower. For five more days it held.
On day sixty-six I felt something pop halfway up the hill. I walked home. The physiotherapist said it was an overuse injury and that I needed to stop completely and do rehab exercises. I didn't run for seven weeks.
When I started again, my stamina was gone. I was back to where I'd been in the first week.
I'm Nilesh, and the streak I was so proud of cost me more days than it ever gave me.

qa.a: Nilesh felt something pop halfway up the hill and walked home.

qa.q: How did Nilesh feel about the streak before the injury?
qa.a: Nilesh felt proud and determined, having posted about sixty days in the college group and laughing off the idea of rest.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Nilesh handled the knee pain?
qa.a: I would follow Zubin's advice and get it seen early, because a few days off would have protected months of training.

qa.q: How might Zubin feel hearing about the injury?
qa.a: Zubin may feel sad and a little frustrated, since the advice to rest and get it checked was ignored.

grounding: Shows a person running through knee pain to protect a streak, leading to an injury that halts training for weeks.
